QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_25

question.text: When a Cat III AIF undergoes a change of Sponsor/Investment Manager, the mandatory exit provision for dissenting close-ended investors can be WAIVED if:

answer.text: The IM promises to refund management fees
75% of unit holders by value of their investment approve the change
The incoming IM provides a one-year performance guarantee

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the CTR and Regulation 20(13)/related circulars, the mandatory exit process for dissenting investors upon change of Sponsor/IM or material PPM change does NOT apply if the AIF has obtained approval of NOT LESS THAN 75% of unit holders by value of their investment. **The Trap:** SEBI dispensation (A) is not a waiver mechanism. Fee refunds (B) and performance guarantees (D) are commercial sweeteners, not regulatory waivers. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the same 75% waiver across categories. XIX-B (distributor) frames from client side. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Run a pre-vote whip to secure > 75% BEFORE formal notice — the mandatory exit process (2-valuer bid + buyout at average) is expensive and distracting. A successful 75% waiver saves cash and time.
